name: Foreign Investor Registration and Automatic Immigrant Quota (GIPC Act)

requirement_groups.name: Joint venture with a Ghanaian partner

requirements.blocker_text: Minimum US$200,000 in cash or capital goods by way of equity participation, with the Ghanaian partner holding at least 10% equity.
requirements.fix_path: Invest at least US$200,000 in equity in a joint venture where a Ghanaian partner holds 10%+.

requirements.blocker_text: Minimum US$500,000 in cash or capital goods by way of equity capital, with no Ghanaian equity partner required.
requirements.fix_path: Invest at least US$500,000 in equity capital.

requirements.blocker_text: Minimum US$1,000,000 in cash or goods/services relevant to the investment.
requirements.fix_path: Invest at least US$1,000,000 in the trading enterprise.

requirements.blocker_text: Must employ at least 20 skilled Ghanaians.
requirements.fix_path: Hire at least 20 skilled Ghanaian employees.

evidence_required.document: Proof of equity capital transfer (cash or capital goods)
Evidence of Ghanaian equity partner (joint venture track)
Payroll/employment records for 20+ skilled Ghanaians (trading track)

outcome.duration_length: not specified in the source located in this build; tied to work/residence permit issued under the GIPC shareholder category

sources.title: Ghana Investment Promotion Centre -- Ghana Investment Promotion Centre Act, 2013 (Act 865): joint venture with a Ghanaian partner requires minimum US$200,000 equity (Ghanaian partner holding 10%+); wholly foreign-owned enterprise requires minimum US$500,000 equity capital; trading enterprises (purchasing/selling imported goods and services) require minimum US$1,000,000 and at least 20 skilled Ghanaian employees

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Ghana). Published on tier-1 sourcing directly from the Ghana Investment Promotion Centre's own hosted copy of the Act. Registration under the GIPC Act is the gateway to the 'GIPC Shareholder' work-and-residence permit category referenced on the Ghana Immigration Service's own site (see gh_work_permit.json's sibling permit family) -- this file models the underlying capital thresholds; the immigration paperwork itself is processed through the same Work and Residence Permit channel used for missionaries/NGOs/immigrant quota. Cleanly tiered by structure (joint venture cheapest, wholly-owned enterprise mid-tier, trading most expensive plus a mandatory local-hiring floor) -- a distinctive, clearly-legislated three-tier capital structure not seen in exactly this form elsewhere in this dataset.
